headline: Attention Is All You Need: The translation problem that led to ChatGPT
summary: The Transformer architecture, now powering models like ChatGPT, was born from a 2017 Google research paper aimed at improving machine translation.
details: In 2017, a Google team was working on machine translation, not chatbots. Their goal was to improve upon Google Translate's neural system, which had recently advanced to translating whole sentences rather than short phrases.

Previous neural translation models read language sequentially, creating a bottleneck for longer sentences and a poor match for modern hardware like GPUs. This sequential processing meant the model had to process word 20 only after processing words 1 through 19.

The breakthrough came with the concept of 'attention,' first introduced in 2014. Attention allowed translation models to look back across source words and assign weight to specific words relevant to the current translation output, loosening the bottleneck.

The 2017 paper, 'Attention Is All You Need,' took this further by proposing the Transformer architecture. It replaced recurrent layers entirely with self-attention mechanisms, allowing every position in the input to attend to every other position.

This parallel processing capability of the Transformer architecture was a significant leap, enabling models to handle longer sequences more efficiently and paving the way for more powerful language models.

The Transformer's ability to process information in parallel, rather than sequentially, was key to its success and became the foundation for subsequent large language models like BERT and eventually ChatGPT.
